items.t: Not all fund managers follow the crowd: Here's a list of stocks that are present in only one mutual fund scheme
sum: Not every stock in a mutual fund portfolio is a popular pick among fund managers. While popular stocks such as HDFC Bank feature in the portfolios of over 700 mutual fund schemes, some companies find a place in just one scheme.
These relatively uncommon stock picks reflect the distinct investment strategies, market views and stock-selection approaches of individual fund managers.

According to data shared by Value Research on X, 13 stocks feature in the portfolios of just one mutual fund scheme each. These include stocks such as Simplex Infrastructures, Ambika Cotton Mills, Tourism Finance Corporation of India and Brooks Laboratories.

The data highlights how fund managers sometimes take relatively uncommon stock bets, allocating a portion of their scheme's assets to equity options that may not be widely held across the mutual fund industry.
The table lists the 13 stocks, their respective mutual fund schemes, and the percentage of each scheme's net assets allocated to the stock.
Source: Value Research; Data as of 30 September 2026. Only stocks with a portfolio weight of at least 1% have been considered.

Simplex Infrastructures has the highest allocation among the listed stocks, accounting for 2.80% of Quant Infrastructure Fund's net assets. Tourism Finance Corporation of India follows with a 2.69% allocation in Union Active Momentum Fund. At the other end, Q-Line Biotech accounts for 1.08% of Abakkus Small Cap Fund's net assets.

sum: Tempsens Instruments shares surged 17% on Tuesday, 3 November, extending their strong post-listing rally. The stock has gained around 89% over its IPO price of ₹300 in just over two months since its listing on 28 August 2026.

The temperature-sensing and heating solutions provider made a stellar debut on the stock exchanges, closing its listing day at a 95.6% premium over the issue price. The stock opened at ₹631.20 on the BSE, up 110.4% from its IPO price, and touched an intraday high of ₹635, representing a gain of 111.66%. It eventually settled at ₹586.80.
With its blockbuster debut, Tempsens Instruments emerged as the year's biggest listing gainer at the time.

Last week, the company reported strong revenue growth in Q2 FY27, with consolidated revenue from operations rising 34% year-on-year to ₹136.31 crore. Revenue also increased 14.8% sequentially, supported by healthy demand across its three business verticals and the consolidation of recently acquired European entities.
For the first half of FY27, revenue grew 33.7% year-on-year to ₹255.02 crore.

However, the company's EBITDA margin contracted to 21.2% in H1 FY27 from 25.2% in the corresponding period last year, reflecting higher operating costs linked to capacity expansion and international acquisitions.
EBITDA increased 8.6% year-on-year to ₹28.32 crore in Q2 FY27, while adjusted profit after tax (PAT) rose 18.5% to ₹20.28 crore.

Massive surge! Reliance Industries shares up 12% after Q2; add ₹2 lakh cr in mcap — when did RIL last rally this much?
sum: The shares finished Monday’s trade with a solid 12% jump to settle at ₹1,300 on NSE, their highest level since early September. The stock last posted a comparable single-day surge in April 2020. Given its heavyweight status in the Nifty 50, the rally also lifted the index by 1.7%, even as tensions in West Asia remained elevated.

For long-term Reliance Industries shareholders, the sharp rise has revived confidence in the stock, which had been trending lower since the start of 2026. The shares closed in the red in eight of the previous 10 months. Despite Monday’s rebound, the stock remains down 17.22% so far this year.

The double-digit jump in the stock added ₹1.84 lakh crore to the company’s market capitalisation, taking it to ₹17.6 lakh crore and helping it retain its position as India’s most valuable listed company.

At its peak of ₹1,611, the company commanded a market capitalisation of ₹21.8 lakh crore. It had crossed the ₹21 lakh crore mark in June 2024, becoming the first Indian company to achieve this milestone.

Meanwhile, investors in the Reliance Group have another reason to celebrate, as its telecom arm, Jio Platforms, made a blockbuster stock market debut last week, listing at ₹1,440 apiece, a premium of 21.3% over its issue price.

Reliance Industries Ltd reported a record consolidated profit after tax (PAT) of ₹29,550 crore for the July-September quarter (Q2 FY27), marking a 33.8% increase from ₹22,092 crore in the year-ago period. Revenue rose 27.8% year-on-year (YoY) to ₹3,62,268 crore, while EBITDA increased 23.9% to a record ₹62,409 crore.

The strong performance was primarily driven by a recovery in the oil-to-chemicals (O2C) business, where EBITDA surged 67.9% to ₹25,203 crore, supported by higher global fuel margins and improved petrochemical spreads. O2C revenue increased 44.2% to ₹2,31,601 crore, with supply disruptions in West Asia and other regions pushing transportation fuel cracks higher.

Jio Platforms vs Bharti Airtel shares: Which telecom stock to buy after Reliance arm’s IPO listing? Experts suggestions
sum: Jio Platforms’ strong market debut has intensified comparisons with Bharti Airtel. Experts view Jio as a higher-growth bet on 5G and digital services, but warn its valuation is demanding. Airtel offers stronger earnings visibility, cash flows and capital discipline.

The listing of Jio Platforms has put the spotlight on India’s telecom sector, with investors now weighing whether the newly listed Reliance Industries-backed company or established rival Bharti Airtel offers a better investment opportunity.

Jio Platforms shares have surged nearly 28% from their issue price of ₹1,119 since making their market debut on Wednesday, 28 October, taking its market capitalisation to nearly ₹13.18 lakh crore and making it India’s second-most valuable listed company after Reliance Industries. The strong debut and subsequent gains follow an IPO that attracted bids for 22.19 times the shares on offer.

Bharti Airtel, meanwhile, has built a strong long-term track record, with its shares delivering returns of 586.10% over the past decade and 187.07% over five years. However, the stock remains down 6.64% so far in 2026. With Jio commanding a substantial valuation and Airtel offering an established earnings track record, which telecom stock should investors consider now? Experts weigh in on their growth prospects, valuations and investment appeal.

Bharti Airtel, meanwhile, remains a stronger proposition for investors seeking earnings visibility, higher ARPU, robust cash flows and disciplined capital allocation. Experts say investors should weigh valuations, earnings growth and execution risks before choosing between the two telecom stocks.

Gaurav Arora, Head of Research at SAHI, said Jio’s listing at a valuation of around ₹10.3 lakh crore places it among India’s top five companies by market capitalisation from day one. This, he said, changes the investment question from assessing the company’s growth potential to evaluating the returns investors can realistically expect from current levels. Companies of this scale rarely grow significantly faster than the broader economy, making low double-digit annual returns a reasonable base case.
He also noted that ARPU growth in India has historically been uneven, with increases largely coming through tariff hikes in 2019, 2021 and 2024.

Adani Enterprises returns to profit as revenue jumps 75%, but shares fall 20%: Can new businesses deliver?
sum: New Delhi, Oct. 29 -- Adani Enterprises Ltd., the flagship company of billionaire Gautam Adani's conglomerate, returned to profit in the September quarter as newer businesses, including airports and data centres, scaled up. But with the stock down more than 20% from its July peak, investors are looking for earnings growth to justify the company's expansion plans.

Net income was Rs.1,490 crore for the three months ended 30 September, according to an exchange filing on Wednesday. While profit was 55% lower than a year earlier, the company returned to the black after reporting a loss of Rs.1,160 crore in the previous quarter amid costs linked to the settlement of US legal cases.
Revenue rose 75% year-on-year to Rs.37,220 crore, while costs increased 71% to Rs.36,020 crore. Gross debt slipped 0.3% from the preceding quarter to Rs.97,294 crore.

The return to profitability could ease investor concerns about funding requirements for expansion and whether newer businesses are approaching an earnings inflection point. Airports, data centres, roads and clean-energy ventures are expected to play a growing role in the company's profit mix as they start generating cash flow.

However, the company needs to deliver on multiple infrastructure projects to fulfil its earnings promise. Its shares have tumbled more than 20% from their July peak, wiping out almost $10 billion in market value. The retreat follows a 43% rally earlier this year after the conglomerate settled multiple regulatory and legal cases in India and the US.

The earlier rally "priced in stronger institutional support, fresh capital and faster earnings growth across Adani Enterprises' emerging businesses," Gary Tan, a portfolio manager at Allspring Global Investments, which holds the stock, told Bloomberg. Now investors have shifted their focus "from growth potential to earnings delivery," he said.
The company's integrated resources management unit, which mostly consists of coal trading and contributes the most to overall revenue, reported a 6.6% increase in revenue to Rs.7,097 crore.

Adani Enterprises revenue jumps 75% as new businesses ramp up; Adani Ports raises FY27 guidance
sum: MUMBAI: Adani Group flagship Adani Enterprises Ltd reported a 75% jump in revenue in the July-September quarter (Q2FY27), buoyed by the ramp-up of copper smelting and the newly built Navi Mumbai airport. Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone Ltd, the group’s key earnings driver, also posted strong growth, with profit rising nearly a fifth from a year earlier.

The results come as the group’s airport business faces a standoff with airlines over plans to shift flights from Mumbai’s main airport to Navi Mumbai ahead of renovations at Terminal 1, scheduled to begin in April 2027.

Adani Airport Holdings Ltd, India’s largest private-sector airport operator with eight airports, is confident it can persuade international airlines to move operations to Navi Mumbai to facilitate the renovation of Terminal 1, chief executive Arun Bansal told analysts on Wednesday.

Discussions remain inconclusive with all but a few international carriers, Bansal said. Several international airlines and the three leading domestic carriers have already announced plans to shift some routes to Navi Mumbai ahead of the renovation.
The company expects the new airport to reach its full annual capacity of 20 million passengers by the end of March 2028. Work on its second phase is set to begin next month, Bansal said.

Adani’s data-centre business also expanded during the quarter. Operational capacity reached 94.6 megawatts, while the company secured fresh orders for another 240 megawatts, taking its tied-up capacity to more than 1.2 gigawatts.

Adani Enterprises’ other businesses include solar-panel and wind-turbine manufacturing, roads, mining and coal trading, alongside copper smelting. The company also serves as an incubator for new businesses within the conglomerate.

Adani Enterprises Drops 6% As Adani Stocks Face Fresh Selling
sum: Adani Enterprises shares slide nearly 6% as broad market weakness, higher crude oil prices and selling across Adani Group stocks weigh on sentiment.

Adani-enterprises-ltd-112599">Adani Enterprises shares were trading at Rs 2,580.60, down 5.92 per cent, at 2:54 pm on October 8, 2026. The stock opened at Rs 2,740 and touched an Intraday low of Rs 2,547, extending its decline for the second consecutive session. The stock had closed at Rs 2,743 on October 7.

The sharp fall in Adani Enterprises comes amid a wider sell-off in Indian equities. The Nifty 50 slipped below 22,500 during the session, while the Sensex also came under heavy pressure. Rising crude oil prices, continued foreign investor selling and the RBI's decision to raise the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50 per cent have weighed on sentiment.

Brent crude moved above USD 100 a barrel as concerns over Middle East supply disruptions intensified. Higher oil prices are a concern for India because they can add to inflation and increase the country's import bill.

The weakness was not limited to Adani Enterprises. Several other Adani Group companies also declined during Thursday's session, with Adani Green Energy, Adani Power and Adani Ports coming under pressure. Adani Enterprises was among the sharper losers in the group.
This suggests that the stock's fall is part of broader selling across the group rather than being driven by a single negative announcement from Adani Enterprises.

Interestingly, the decline came just a day after Adani Enterprises received a positive credit-rating development. CARE Ratings upgraded the company's long-term rating to CARE AA; Stable from CARE AA-; Stable, while reaffirming its short-term rating at CARE A1+.

sum: CARE Ratings has also reaffirmed the company's short-term rating at CARE A1+.

"We would like to inform you the following updates on credit ratings by CARE Ratings Limited. AEL’s long-term rating is now upgraded to AA Stable, highest-ever rating in its credit history," Adani Enterprises said.
The company said the upgrade "serves as an independent validation of AEL’s disciplined capital management and tight fiscal prudence".

"AEL has constantly strengthened its credit profile over the last 7 years whilst executing an ever-increasing core infrastructure-led capex. AEL’s stronger credit further enhances resilience of its unique incubation platform and assures long-term value for its stakeholders," the company said.

"Upgrade reflects the strengthened financial risk profile of AEL following equity raise of Rs 15,000 crore through qualified institutional placement (QIP) in July 2026 and execution of subscription agreement for the sale of 5.54% stake in its wholly owned subsidiary Adani Airports Holdings Limited (AAHL) at a pre-money valuation of Rs 1.67 lakh crore, thus significantly enhancing financial flexibility for AEL," CARE Ratings said.
AAHL expects to receive Rs 9,825 crore by July 2027 from the stake sale, the rating agency added.

In CareEdge Ratings' opinion, the strengthened financial flexibility of the Adani group, along with the promoter family's substantial ownership across key group entities, enhances the strategic importance of Adani Enterprises and the promoters' economic incentive to support its diverse ventures in case of exigencies.

sum: New Delhi, Sept. 28 -- Adani Enterprises shares dropped 2% in the morning trade on the BSE on Monday, 28 September, after Adani Group entities executed a bulk deal of 86 lakh shares on Friday.

Adani Enterprises' share price opened at Rs.2,922.50 against its previous close of Rs.2,914.95 and declined 2% to an intraday low of Rs.2,856. However, it pared some losses, as around 10 am, the stock was 1.35% down at Rs.2,875.60.

NSE bulk deal data for Friday, 25 September, showed that 86 lakh shares changed hands between promoter group entities of Adani Enterprises in a deal worth Rs.2,498 crore through separate block deals on Friday.

As per the NSE data, Adani Infra (India) bought 34,50,000 shares in the group's flagship company Adani Enterprises at an average price of Rs.2,905 per share, while Adani Properties acquired 51,50,000 shares of Adani Enterprises at the same price, taking the combined deal value to Rs.2,498.30 crore for 86,00,000 shares.
On the other side of the trades, promoter group entity Infinite Trade And Investment Ltd sold an equal number of shares at the same price.
The share sale has trimmed Infinite Trade And Investment's holding in Adani Enterprises to 1.38% from 2.01% earlier.
In the last six months, the stock has jumped 57% compared to a nearly 1% decline in the equity benchmark Sensex. Year-to-date, it is up 27% against a 14% decline in the Sensex.

sum: Adani group stocks: Following a management meet, Jefferies recommended a 'Buy' rating on Adani Power, Adani Green Energy, Adani Energy Solutions and Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone.

Adani group shares were in demand, rallying up to 15 per cent on the BSE in Friday’s intra-day deals after brokerage firm Jefferies recommended a ‘Buy’ rating on four group stocks, namely Adani Power, Adani Green Energy, Adani Energy Solutions and Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone (SEZ). Analysts at the brokerage firm took Adani group company’s management view at Jefferies India Forum 2026.

Among the listed Adani group stocks, Adani Total Gas (ATGL) soared 15 per cent on the back of eight-fold jump in the average trading volume. A combined 32.71 million shares changed hands on the NSE and BSE.

Share price Adani Green Energy surged 6 per cent to ₹1,338.05, followed by Adani Energy Solutions (4 per cent at ₹1,437), Adani Enterprises (3 per cent at ₹3,005), Adani Power (2 per cent at ₹209.60) and Adani Ports (2 per cent at ₹1,779.75). In comparison, the BSE Sensex was up 0.41 per cent at 74,622 at 02:25 PM.
Jefferies recommend a ‘Buy’ rating on Adani Energy Solutions with a target price (TP) of ₹2,060 per share.

Adani Energy Solutions’ management remains upbeat on prospects of its Trading business. They further highlighted that India’s transmission outlook remains robust and reiterated their guidance on medium-term annual capex run-rate of ₹20,000-25,000 crore. Smart meters and trading business is ramping up well and will be the key growth drivers going forward, the brokerage firm said.

Meanwhile, Adani Green Energy’s management remains confident of adding 5 GW capacity in FY27E. The company is aligning capacity addition timelines with transmission infrastructure to mitigate curtailment risk. Plans to ramp up Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) capacity from 3.6 GWh currently to 10 GWh+ by FY27E remain on track. Capacity tie-up with Adani Energy Solutions caps merchant upside, though improves earnings predictability, the brokerage firm said, while assinging a TP of ₹1,695 per share.

sum: Stock to buy: Finolex Cables share price has surged nearly 16% in the last week. The wires and cables maker is likely to benefit from its backward integration, capacity build-out across fibre, and strong data centres-led OFC demand, highlighted InCred Equities in its latest report.
The brokerage is likely to see an upward revision once the Finolex Cables expanded capacities fall in place and ramp up to full utilisation.

Finolex Cables remain India's only wire and cable player with in-house continuous copper-rod casting and currently stands as India's second optical-fibre preform producer.

Commissioning of its Vapour Axial Deposition-based plant also helped in reducing import dependence. While the data-centre demand would provide a meaningful growth to the company, its distribution expansion is likely to complement disciplined allocation.
The brokerage maintained an ‘Add’ rating for the stock with a target price of ₹1,435 per share.

sum: Adani Airport Holdings Limited (AAHL), a subsidiary of Adani Enterprises Limited (AEL) and one of India's largest private airport operators, has entered into binding agreements to raise ₹9,825 crore (nearly $1 billion) of primary equity capital from a consortium of investors.
Adani Airport Holdings Ltd (AAHL), a subsidiary of Adani Enterprises, operates eight airports in India. Image: https://www.adanienterprises.com/businesses/airports

It comprises Alpha Wave Global, Premji Invest, Temasek and BlackRock managed funds. The transaction values AAHL at a pre-money equity valuation of nearly $18 billion and represents one of the largest primary equity investments from financial institutions in India’s airport infrastructure sector.

The press release said the participation of a consortium of long-term domestic and global investors represents a significant institutional endorsement of AAHL’s scale, operating capabilities and long-term growth potential. The investment brings long-duration institutional capital into the business at a time when India’s aviation sector is entering a sustained phase of passenger growth, capacity expansion and infrastructure investment.

The proceeds will support three strategic priorities: expanding and modernising airport infrastructure across AAHL’s portfolio; accelerating the development of integrated Adani Airport City ecosystems around its airports with development of ~ 22 million sq. ft. of mixed-use development planned in the first phase; and scaling passenger-facing and other non-aeronautical businesses including our ground handling business.

These investments are expected to increase capacity to serve nearly 200 million passengers annually, deepen commercial monetisation, enhance passenger experience and further strengthen AAHL’s integrated airport ecosystem, it added.

“This partnership marks an important milestone in building out the Adani Airports platform, and we are privileged to have such marquee, long-term investors alongside us on this journey,” said Jeet Adani, Non-Executive Director, Adani Airport Holdings Limited. “India’s aviation sector is one of the most powerful multipliers of the country’s GDP growth.
